prompt.context_jp: 画面に表示されているのは、その日、会社で思いがけない行動に出てしまった相手、手嶋の名前だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 画面に表示されているの___、手嶋の名前だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits. The 'name displayed on the screen' is being identified.

feedback.correct_en: は marks the topic 'what is displayed on the screen,' with the identifying predicate '手嶋の名前だった' providing new information. This is a classic 'as for X, it is Y' identification pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly flip the structure and lose the topic–comment identification; here the screen content is already the discourse frame.

contrast_examples.jp: 画面に表示されているのは手嶋の名前だった。
contrast_examples.en: What was on the screen was Tejima's name. (topic–identification)

contrast_examples.jp: 画面に手嶋の名前が表示されていた。
contrast_examples.en: Tejima's name was displayed on the screen. (new-info が)

prompt.context_jp: 恋愛が苦手な自分にとって、電話越しの沈黙ほど心細いものはない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 恋愛___苦手な自分にとって、電話越しの沈黙ほど心細いものはない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits inside the relative clause describing 'self'.

feedback.correct_en: In the 〜が苦手 pattern, the thing one is bad at is marked by が — it identifies the object of the stative adjective. Inside the relative clause modifying 自分, は would break the subordinate structure.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would promote 恋愛 to a main-clause topic, but here the phrase is embedded inside 〜な自分 describing Hotaru.

contrast_examples.en: I'm bad at romance. (が marks what one is bad at)
Romance — (I'm) bad at it. (contrastive topic)

prompt.context_jp: ちゃぶ台の向こうでは、高野が新聞を広げたまま、明らかにこちらの様子をうかがっていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: ちゃぶ台の向こうで___、高野が新聞を広げたまま、明らかにこちらの様子をうかがっていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle attached to the location phrase.

feedback.correct_en: で+は sets 'on the other side of the chabudai' as a contrastive scene-setting topic — Hotaru is on the phone here, while over there Takano is eavesdropping. が cannot attach to a で-phrase like this.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would be ungrammatical after で as a scene-setter; the sentence needs topic/contrast marking.

contrast_examples.jp: 居間では母が本を読んでいた。
contrast_examples.en: In the living room, Mom was reading. (scene-setting contrast)
A dog is barking in the yard. (simple location + new-info が)

prompt.context_jp: 受話口の向こうにまで届きそうなくらい、鼓動が大きかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 心臓の音___、受話口の向こうまで聞こえてしまいそうだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 'the sound of her heart.'

feedback.correct_en: The heartbeat is newly spotlighted as a vivid sensation — が presents it as the salient new subject she's suddenly aware of.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame 'the heartbeat' as an already established topic, which clashes with the sudden-realization feel here.

contrast_examples.en: I can hear my heartbeat. (new realization)

contrast_examples.jp: 心臓の音は普段は聞こえない。
contrast_examples.en: Normally you don't hear your heartbeat. (contrastive topic)

prompt.context_jp: 電話を切ったあとも、蛍の頬はしばらく緩みっぱなしだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 電話を切ったあとも、蛍の頬___しばらく緩みっぱなしだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 'Hotaru's cheeks.'

feedback.correct_en: Hotaru is the ongoing topic of the scene; her cheeks are being described as part of her state. は fits the topic-comment description of a continuing state.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight the cheeks as new information, but we are describing Hotaru's lingering emotional state, not introducing her cheeks.

contrast_examples.en: Her cheeks were red. (description of known entity)
Her cheeks suddenly turned red. (new event)

prompt.context_jp: 居間の静けさを破るように、庭から音が聞こえた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 縁側の風鈴___、夜風に揺れてちりんと鳴った。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the wind chime.

feedback.correct_en: The wind chime is introduced here as a fresh sensory event — が presents new information in a scene-description sentence.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply the wind chime was already an established topic, but here it enters the scene for the first time.

contrast_examples.en: A wind chime rang. (new event)
Wind chimes are a summer tradition. (general topic)

prompt.context_jp: 自分の恋がようやく動き出した一方で、この人は別居中の妻との問題を抱えたままなのだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 自分の恋___ようやく動き出した一方で、この人は別居中の妻との問題を抱えたままなのだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 'my own love.'

feedback.correct_en: Inside the 〜一方で subordinate clause, が marks the subject neutrally. The contrastive pairing is handled at the clause level, not by は on 恋.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside this subordinate clause would clash — the main contrast marker は is already carried by この人 in the main clause.

contrast_examples.jp: 雨が降る一方で、風も吹いていた。
contrast_examples.en: While rain was falling, the wind was also blowing.

contrast_examples.jp: 私は本を読み、彼は音楽を聴いた。
contrast_examples.en: I read a book, and he listened to music. (contrastive は)

prompt.context_jp: 部屋には、柱時計の振り子の音だけが響いている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 部屋には、柱時計の振り子の音だけ___響いている。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits after 'only the pendulum sound.'

feedback.correct_en: '〜だけが' exhaustively identifies the one and only thing filling the silence — classic exhaustive-listing が.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは would imply contrast ('only this, in contrast to something else') but here we want 'nothing but this sound.'

contrast_examples.en: You alone are my only hope. (exhaustive が)
You, at least, I believe in. (contrastive は)

prompt.context_jp: 蛍が自分の部屋へ引き上げると、居間には高野一人が残された。
prompt.prompt_jp: 蛍が自分の部屋へ引き上げると、居間には高野一人___残された。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking '高野一人' (Takano alone).

feedback.correct_en: が exhaustively picks out Takano as the sole person left — 'one person, namely Takano, was left.' This is new, salient information after Hotaru exits.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make Takano a continuing topic, but the sentence focuses on who is now the only one remaining.

contrast_examples.jp: 部屋には私一人が残された。
contrast_examples.en: Only I was left in the room. (exhaustive が)
I stayed behind by myself. (topic は)

prompt.context_jp: 周囲は休暇気分で浮かれているなか、高野だけはいつも通り。
prompt.prompt_jp: 高野だけ___相変わらず淡々と書類に目を通し、部下の差し出す書類に判を押している。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after '高野だけ'.

feedback.correct_en: '〜だけは' sets up a strong contrast — everyone else is giddy, but Takano alone stays calm. The contrastive は is what gives the sentence its 'only he, unlike the others' feel.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけが would exhaustively name him as the one doing some action; here the author wants contrast with the surrounding colleagues, which は carries.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼だけは落ち着いていた。
contrast_examples.en: He alone (unlike others) was calm. (contrastive は)

contrast_examples.jp: 彼だけが正解を知っていた。
contrast_examples.en: He alone knew the answer. (exhaustive が)

prompt.context_jp: 「私の妻のことはいい 君の話だ｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私の妻のこと___いい、君の話だ。
prompt.prompt_en: Takano brushes aside the topic of his own wife. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: は here is contrastive: 'as for my wife — never mind that; we're talking about you.' The particle signals a deliberate shift away from one topic to another.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 'my wife's matter' the new-info subject, losing the dismissive 'set that aside' nuance.

contrast_examples.jp: それはいい。今は君の話だ。
contrast_examples.en: Forget that. Right now we're talking about you.
That's a good one. (new-info が, totally different meaning)

prompt.context_jp: せっかく二人きりになれたというのに、蛍の頭の中は真っ白だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: せっかく二人きりになれたというのに、蛍の頭の中___真っ白だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 'inside Hotaru's head.'

feedback.correct_en: Hotaru is the ongoing topic; the comment describes the state of her mind. は frames the body-part-of-topic for a stative description.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 'her mind' the newly introduced subject, but she's the established protagonist and we're describing a familiar state.

contrast_examples.en: My mind is blank. (describing one's state)
Something came to mind. (new event)

prompt.context_jp: いつもなら黙っていても出てくる伝票やコーヒーが、今日は何ひとつ出てこない。
prompt.prompt_jp: いつもなら黙っていても出てくる伝票やコーヒー___、今日は何ひとつ出てこない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 'the forms and coffee that would normally appear.'

feedback.correct_en: が neutrally marks the subject of the embedded relative-style description, and the contrast is carried by 今日は in the main clause.
feedback.incorrect_en: は here would awkwardly double-topic the sentence, since 今日は already provides the contrastive frame.

contrast_examples.jp: いつも出る物が、今日は出ない。
contrast_examples.en: What usually comes out doesn't today. (が + contrastive は)
The forms, today, don't come out. (double は sounds heavy)

prompt.context_jp: お盆休みを目前に控えたある夜、蛍は古い一軒家の居間で携帯電話を握りしめていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 蛍は古い一軒家の居間で携帯電話___握りしめていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 'cellphone.'

feedback.correct_en: 握りしめる is a transitive verb; the thing gripped takes を as the direct object.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would turn the phone into the subject (and clash with 蛍は), while に doesn't fit a transitive 'grip' action.

contrast_examples.en: To clutch a letter tightly.
To hold a pen.

prompt.context_jp: 高野はネクタイを緩めながら居間に上がり、座布団にどっかりと腰を下ろした。
prompt.prompt_jp: 高野はネクタイを緩めながら居間___上がり、座布団にどっかりと腰を下ろした。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'the living room' as destination.

feedback.correct_en: 上がる (to step up into a Japanese room) takes に to mark the destination of the movement.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark a location of action, not the goal; を doesn't fit with 上がる in this sense.

contrast_examples.en: To step up into the room.
To rest in the room. (location of activity)

prompt.context_jp: 何か気の利いたことを言わんとするたびに、喉の奥で言葉が絡まってしまう。
prompt.prompt_jp: 何か気の利いたことを言わんとするたびに、喉の奥で言葉が___しまう。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the verb that fits the idiom 'words get ___ in the back of the throat.'

feedback.correct_en: 言葉が絡まる ('words get tangled') is the set collocation for being tongue-tied — exactly the nervous feeling Hotaru has.
feedback.incorrect_en: 転ぶ (to fall over) and 折れる (to break) aren't idiomatic with 言葉 in this nervousness sense.

contrast_examples.jp: 緊張して言葉が絡まる。
contrast_examples.en: I get tongue-tied from nerves.
One's tongue gets twisted. (similar idiom)

prompt.context_jp: 蛍は一度大きく息を吸い込み、ようやく口を開いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 蛍は一度大きく息を___、ようやく口を開いた。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the verb for 'drawing in a big breath.'

feedback.correct_en: 息を吸い込む is the natural collocation for drawing breath in deeply before speaking.
feedback.incorrect_en: 引き取る means to take custody / to retreat; 押し込む means to shove into — neither pairs with 息 in this way.

contrast_examples.en: To inhale deeply.
To exhale.

prompt.context_jp: 普段は誰に対しても隙を見せない上司が、その話になると途端に口数が少なくなることを、蛍はもう知っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 普段は誰に対しても___を見せない上司
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the word meaning a 'opening' or vulnerability in one's guard.

feedback.correct_en: 隙を見せる ('to show an opening / a gap in one's guard') is the fixed phrase for letting one's defenses down.
feedback.incorrect_en: 穴 (hole) and 傷 (wound) don't form the idiom 'show vulnerability' with 見せる.

contrast_examples.en: He has no openings — a flawless/guarded person.
To show an opening to your opponent.

prompt.context_jp: 余計なお世話だと分かっていても、黙っていられないのが蛍という人間だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: ___お世話だと分かっていても、黙っていられないのが蛍という人間だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the adjective that fits with お世話 for 'unnecessary meddling.'

feedback.correct_en: 余計なお世話 is a set expression meaning 'none of your business / unnecessary meddling.' Hotaru recognizes she's overstepping.
feedback.incorrect_en: 無駄なお世話 and 大きなお世話 vary in nuance — 大きなお世話 does exist but is a retort; 余計な is the idiomatic self-reflective form used here.

contrast_examples.jp: それは余計なお世話だ。
contrast_examples.en: That's none of your business.
Mind your own business! (retort)

prompt.context_jp: 張り詰めていたフロアの空気が、ふっと緩んだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 張り詰めていたフロアの空気が、ふっと___。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the verb that pairs with 空気 (atmosphere) for 'relaxed.'

feedback.correct_en: 空気が緩む is the natural collocation for a tense atmosphere easing up.
feedback.incorrect_en: 空気が落ちる doesn't work idiomatically; 壊れる would mean the atmosphere was ruined — wrong nuance for relief.

contrast_examples.en: Tension eases.
The atmosphere freezes (becomes awkward).

prompt.context_jp: 「いきなり核心を突いて来たな｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: いきなり核心を___来たな。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the verb meaning 'strike at the heart of the matter.'

feedback.correct_en: 核心を突く ('to strike/pierce the core') is the set idiom for getting straight to the point.
feedback.incorrect_en: 叩く (strike repeatedly) and 押す (push) don't form idioms with 核心.

contrast_examples.en: A question that hits the core.
To hit the mark (similar idiom).

prompt.context_jp: 張り詰めていたものが一気にほどけ、膝から力が抜けていくようだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 張り詰めていたものが一気に___、膝から力が抜けていくようだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the verb meaning 'came undone / unraveled.'

feedback.correct_en: 張り詰めたものがほどける is the idiomatic image of tension untying itself, like a tightly wound string being released.
feedback.incorrect_en: 壊れる (break) and 割れる (crack/split) are too violent and don't capture the gentle release of tension.

contrast_examples.en: The tension unravels/eases.
One's heart loosens up.

prompt.context_jp: 高野はついにしびれを切らし、扉を拳で軽くたたいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 高野はついに___を切らし、扉を拳で軽くたたいた。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the noun that completes the idiom 'to lose patience.'

feedback.correct_en: しびれを切らす is the set phrase for 'to run out of patience' — literally 'to cut off the pins-and-needles.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 息を切らす means 'be out of breath'; 気を切らす isn't a set idiom for impatience.

contrast_examples.jp: 待ちくたびれてしびれを切らす。
contrast_examples.en: Get tired of waiting and lose patience.
Run and get out of breath.

prompt.context_jp: Describing Hotaru's mind going blank once she's alone with Teshima.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural in narration?

choices.text: 蛍の頭の中は真っ白だった。
蛍の頭の中が真っ白だった。

feedback.correct_en: Describing the known protagonist's mental state uses は — topic-comment is the default for stative description of a familiar referent.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight 'her head' as newly introduced, which clashes with the fact that Hotaru is the ongoing viewpoint.

contrast_examples.en: My mind is a blank. (describing one's state)

contrast_examples.jp: 急に頭が真っ白になった。
contrast_examples.en: Suddenly my mind went blank. (new-event が)

prompt.context_jp: Hotaru teasingly imitates how Takano should confess to his wife.
prompt.prompt_en: Which casual imitation line fits Hotaru's playful teasing of her boss?

choices.text: 君が好きだもん、君を失いたくないもん。
あなたのことを愛しております。

feedback.correct_en: The 〜だもん ending is deliberately childish and casual — Hotaru is caricaturing an unlikely confession, which is why Takano protests 'I don't talk like that.'
feedback.incorrect_en: The formal 愛しております would completely miss the joke — the humor comes from the mismatch between Takano's stiffness and the babyish だもん.

contrast_examples.en: Cuz I like you. (childish/cute)
I hold you in deep affection. (very formal)

prompt.context_jp: Takano brushes Hotaru off and tells her to worry about her own love life.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line better matches Takano's gruff boss-to-subordinate tone?

choices.text: 君は自分のことだけ心配してろ。
あなたは自分のことだけ心配してください。

feedback.correct_en: The blunt imperative 〜してろ plus 君 matches Takano's clipped, superior tone in private — he's being dismissive, not polite.
feedback.incorrect_en: The ください + あなた version would sound too soft and formal for how Takano actually speaks to Hotaru in this scene.

contrast_examples.en: Shut up / stay quiet. (blunt)
Please be quiet. (polite)

prompt.context_jp: Describing a sudden sensory event in the garden scene.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural as a scene-setting beat?

choices.text: 縁側の風鈴が、夜風に揺れてちりんと鳴った。
縁側の風鈴は、夜風に揺れてちりんと鳴った。

feedback.correct_en: For a one-shot sensory event introducing a new element into the scene, が is the default marker. It presents the chime freshly.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame the wind chime as an already-known topic, which doesn't fit this sudden descriptive moment.

contrast_examples.en: A cat meowed. (new event)
That cat meows a lot. (topic description)

prompt.context_jp: Hotaru, trying to sound like a composed adult, suggests leaving.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing fits a hesitant suggestion between two people who aren't close yet?

choices.text: じゃあ、私達も帰ります？

feedback.correct_en: 帰ります？ with rising intonation is a soft, tentative suggestion appropriate between new acquaintances — exactly what Hotaru is attempting.
feedback.incorrect_en: 帰るぞ is gruff masculine speech, completely wrong for Hotaru trying to come across as a 'nice adult woman' on a date.

contrast_examples.en: Shall we head back now? (soft suggestion)
We're heading back now. (assertive masculine)
